description: we are engineering a 3-layer spacesuit. The outer shield (1mm) features an innovative composite using recycled Biochar from Algerian forest fires, Optical Silicone, Nano-Ceramics, and Mylar. Physics simulation proves ultrafast ESD dissipation (<1.1 ms), outperforming NASA standards. Built using ultrasonic cutting and welding to ensure zero-leakage, complete astronaut safety, and absolute protection for high-value space assets.
summary: Flashcube 110 is a sustainable, zero-operating-cost Lunar Biodome architecture designed for In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU). Our project features a 50m x 4m x 3m long corridor habitat that autonomously extracts lunar water using Flash Joule Heating, yielding an estimated 33.3 tons annually. To ensure absolute safety against electrostatic discharge (ESD) and radiation, we developed a novel 'Biochar-Bronze Puzzle Grid'. This interlocking floor system uses recycled rubber, biochar, and bronze spring connectors to dissipate high voltages seamlessly without epoxy. This innovation not only protects lunar equipment but also serves as a commercial Earth spin-off for critical terrestrial industries like nuclear labs and hospitals, saving an estimated $1.62 billion over 10 years.

1. The Challenge

Watch our Demo Video here

https://youtu.be/Ni2QnySM6V4?si=H3QV9nkOiJyrg6gr

Future lunar missions face two critical hurdles: the high cost of transporting water and the severe threat of Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) from lunar dust, which can easily destroy sensitive electronics and life-support systems.

2. Our Solution: Flashcube 110 & The Puzzle Grid

We designed "Flashcube 110", a sustainable 50m x 4m x 3m Lunar Biodome corridor. It utilizes a micro-excavator and Flash Joule Heating to extract water directly from lunar regolith, yielding approximately 33.3 tons of water annually and saving $1.62 billion in payload costs over a 10-year lifecycle.

To solve the ESD threat, we engineered an unprecedented grounding architecture: The "Biochar-Bronze Puzzle Grid".

3. How It Works

Unlike traditional epoxy-based floors, our modular grid uses interlocking tiles made from recycled rubber and highly conductive Biochar. The true innovation lies in the electro-mechanical contact mechanism: each tile is connected via 4-way bronze spring connectors (functioning like battery terminals) and internal bronze rods. This creates a seamless, 100% continuous grounding network that instantly dissipates high voltages directly into an 80cm deep bronze grounding rod.

4. Earth Spin-Off & Commercial Viability

Beyond the Moon, this ESD grid is a TRL-ready commercial product. It provides zero-downtime, epoxy-free, ultra-durable grounding solutions for Earth’s most critical environments, including NASA electronics labs, nuclear facilities, and hospital operating rooms.
